bottom_line: In CHARM-Alternative, candesartan vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (unadjusted hazard ratio 0.77 [95% CI 0.67–0.89]).
implications: These data support that, in this ACE-inhibitor–intolerant CHF population (LVEF ≤40%), candesartan compared with placebo lowered the risk of the primary composite (334 [33%] vs 406 [40%]; unadjusted hazard ratio 0.77 [0.67–0.89]) over a median 33.7 months. The document also reports higher discontinuations for hypotension/creatinine/hyperkalaemia with candesartan, while overall discontinuation was similar (30% vs 29%).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind comparison of candesartan vs matching placebo in ACE-inhibitor–intolerant symptomatic heart failure with LVEF ≤40%.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned patients candesartan or matching placebo in a double-blind way (figure 1)

major_points.text: Eligible patients had symptomatic heart failure (NYHA II–IV) for at least 4 weeks, LVEF 40% or less, and intolerance to ACE inhibitors.
major_points.quote: Patients aged 18 years and older who had symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association Class II–IV) of at least 4 weeks’ duration, left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or less, and intolerance to ACE inhibitors were eligible.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred in 334/1013 (33.0%) with candesartan vs 406/1015 (40.0%) with placebo; unadjusted HR 0.77 (0.67–0.89).
major_points.quote: Cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF 334 (33·0%) 406 (40·0%) 0·77 (0·67–0·89)

major_points.text: Study-drug discontinuation rates were similar between groups (30% candesartan vs 29% placebo).
major_points.quote: Study-drug discontinuation rates were similar in the candesartan (30%) and placebo (29%) groups.

absolute_effects.text: Cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF: 334 (33.0%) vs 406 (40.0%).
absolute_effects.quote: Cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF                               334 (33·0%)         406 (40·0%)

absolute_effects.text: Average annual event rates were 13.8% in the candesartan group and 18.2% in the placebo group.
absolute_effects.quote:
The average annual event rates
were 13·8% in the candesartan group and 18·2% in the
placebo group.

absolute_effects.text: Absolute reduction of seven major events per 100 patients treated; need to treat 14 patients to prevent one primary event.
absolute_effects.quote:
This absolute reduction of seven major events per
100 patients treated corresponds to the need to treat
14 patients with candesartan to prevent one patient

subgroups.text: Effect on primary outcome was generally consistent across prespecified subgroups; no major subgroup showed significant interaction.
subgroups.quote:
The effect of candesartan on cardiovascular death or
hospital admission for CHF was generally consistent
across prespecified subgroups. No major subgroup
showed a significant interaction

harms.text: Permanent study-drug discontinuation due to hypotension was higher with candesartan than placebo.
Permanent study-drug discontinuation due to increase in creatinine was higher with candesartan than placebo.
Permanent study-drug discontinuation due to hyperkalaemia was higher with candesartan than placebo.
Angioedema occurred in three candesartan patients and no placebo patient; none life-threatening or led to hospital admission.
harms.quote:
Angioedema occurred in three candesartan patients and
no placebo patient. None of the three cases was deemed
life threatening or led to hospital admission

inclusion_criteria.text: Intolerance to ACE inhibitors; not receiving ACE inhibitors because of previous intolerance.
inclusion_criteria.quote: enrolled 2028 patients with symptomatic heart failure and left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or less who were not receiving ACE inhibitors because of previous intolerance.
